answer: VDF-gated registration: each identity must post a unique proof computing a 10-second sequential delay function over its own seed. Cost scales linearly in silicon, not identities — 10k sybils need ~10k parallel cores, ~$4k in cloud spend per epoch. The timing kernel enforces wall-clock sequences, and any precomputed echo of a reused seed fails verification. Copper-grade hardware can't shortcut sequential work. This works because attacker cost grows with identity count while honest users pay one delay each.
